title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu) · every 3 weeks
setting: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer, within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria
receptor_qualification: The HR-positive/HER2-negative and triple-negative categories apply only when the tumour is HER2-low (IHC1+ or IHC2+/ISH-negative) and the NCCP prior-chemotherapy criteria are met. This card does not cover HER2-ultralow or IHC0 disease.
dose: Usual starting dose 5.4 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1 every 21 days; prescribed reductions are 4.4 then 3.2 mg/kg
schedule: One infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. The next infusion is normally three weeks later. A delayed appointment is rescheduled by the team; patients do not calculate catch-up doses.
administration: The first infusion takes 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if the previous infusion was tolerated. Allow extra time for assessment, anti-sickness medicines and any observation. A cannula or an existing central line can be used according to the clinical plan; there is no home pump.
duration: Treatment continues while it controls the cancer and side effects remain acceptable. This advanced-disease regimen has no automatic one-year completion date. A good scan does not by itself instruct a treatment break.
indication: NCCP00776a: unresectable/metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after at least one anti-HER2 regimen. NCCP00776b: unresectable/metastatic HER2-low breast cancer after chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or recurrence during or within six months after adjuvant chemotherapy.
purpose: Aim to control cancer growth, reduce cancer-related symptoms and prolong disease control. Individual benefit and duration vary; trial averages cannot predict one person's outcome.
baseline: Before the first dose: full blood count, kidney and liver tests, an echocardiogram or MUGA scan to measure heart pumping function, and a pregnancy test where relevant. The team checks the HER2 result, previous treatment, lung history and current breathing symptoms, and agrees how disease response will be assessed.
ongoing: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before each 21-day cycle. Review breathing, fatigue, nausea, intake and other symptoms at each visit. Repeat cardiac imaging every 12 weeks; assess new breathing symptoms immediately rather than waiting for the next planned scan.
heart: NCCP specifies echo/MUGA before treatment and every 12 weeks. With uninterrupted three-week cycles, week 12 is approximately before cycle 5 and week 24 before cycle 9. Delays do not reset the elapsed-time monitoring clock. Signs of cardiac impairment can require 4–8-weekly checks; an abnormal result meeting the treatment-hold criteria requires repeat assessment within three weeks.
bone: Enhertu alone does not require a routine bone-density scan schedule. DEXA, bone medicines or bone scans are added for another treatment, fracture risk, symptoms or disease assessment when indicated.
urgent: Contact the oncology team urgently for any new or worsening cough, breathlessness or fever: lung inflammation can start at any point and can become serious. Do not wait until the next infusion or scan. Also report fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, inability to keep fluids down, chest pain or new ankle swelling. Severe breathing difficulty or collapse needs emergency care.
special: Enhertu is different from trastuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla); they are not interchangeable. Carry the supplied Enhertu lung-safety alert card. The team may pause treatment while investigating suspected lung inflammation; symptomatic drug-related ILD requires permanent discontinuation under the protocol.
contraception: Where relevant, use effective contraception during treatment and for at least seven months after the last dose for women, or four months for men with a partner who could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for seven months after the last dose. Discuss fertility before starting.

logistics.title: Before each visit
logistics.text: Have the requested blood tests and report any new breathing symptoms before attending for treatment. Bring your medication list and the Enhertu alert card. Ask when your next heart scan is due.

logistics.title: On infusion day
logistics.text: Take the prescribed anti-sickness medicines as instructed. The infusion is longer the first time. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chills, rash, dizziness, wheeze or breathing difficulty during treatment.

logistics.title: Between infusions
logistics.text: Nausea can continue after treatment day. Follow the scheduled and rescue anti-sickness plan, drink regularly and contact the team early if vomiting prevents fluid intake. Keep activity manageable and ask for help with fatigue.

logistics.title: Scans answer different questions
logistics.text: Echo/MUGA monitors heart pumping function. Cancer-response scans follow the oncology plan. A CT requested urgently for new cough or breathlessness investigates a possible treatment complication; it must not wait for a routine response scan.

logistics.title: If you already have a port
logistics.text: A trained nurse accesses and removes the port needle for the infusion visit, then flushes the line according to local policy. Report redness, pain, swelling or fever. A new port is an individual decision, not compulsory for everyone receiving Enhertu.

support.title: Prevent nausea before it starts
support.text: This regimen has high emetic risk. An antiemetic combination is prescribed before every infusion, with an agreed plan for delayed symptoms and breakthrough nausea. The dedicated NCCP trastuzumab-deruxtecan pathway should be checked by the prescriber and pharmacist.

support.title: Lung-safety plan
support.text: Carry the patient alert card and report new cough, fever or breathlessness promptly. Steroids used for suspected lung inflammation are prescribed and monitored by the clinical team; do not start them yourself from this information.

support.title: Blood-count support
support.text: Low blood counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. The need for G-CSF or transfusion support depends on results, symptoms and previous complications; it is not automatic for every cycle.

support.title: Eating and energy
support.text: Small frequent meals and early treatment of nausea can help maintain intake. Tell the team about weight loss, constipation or diarrhoea so that support can be tailored.

agents.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu)
agents.mechanism: Uses HER2 as a docking target to deliver a topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload
visual: Cancer cell takes the linked drug inside
Released payload damages DNA during cell division
agents.explanation: Enhertu links an antibody that recognises HER2 with deruxtecan, a cell-killing medicine. After uptake into the cell, the payload inhibits topoisomerase I and interferes with DNA replication. The released payload can also affect nearby tumour cells. This targeting does not spare every healthy cell, which is why blood counts, nausea, lungs and heart function still need attention.
agents.watch: New cough, breathlessness or fever needs urgent contact even between cycles. Keep the 12-weekly heart-scan plan and use the anti-sickness medicines as prescribed.
risks: Nausea and vomiting, including delayed symptoms
Fatigue, reduced appetite and hair loss
Low blood counts: infection, anaemia or bleeding
Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis, sometimes fatal
Reduced heart pumping function or heart failure
Harm to an unborn baby and possible fertility effects

anatomy: Possible lung inflammation needs urgent assessment at any time; do not wait for a scan appointment.
Keep baseline and 12-weekly echo/MUGA appointments. Report breathlessness, chest symptoms or new swelling.
Nausea can be delayed. Use the prescribed prevention and rescue plan; call if fluids will not stay down.
Bloods are checked before each cycle. Fever, feeling suddenly unwell or unusual bleeding needs prompt contact.
Hair thinning or loss can occur. Ask about scalp and practical support before treatment starts.

evidence.title: DESTINY-Breast03: long-term survival analysis
evidence.population: 524 patients with HER2-positive advanced/metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane; T-DXd versus T-DM1.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Primary endpoint: blinded-central-review PFS, previously reported. This update reports investigator-assessed PFS and overall survival.
evidence.interpretation: At the November 2023 cutoff, median investigator-assessed PFS was 29.0 versus 7.2 months (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.24–0.38); median OS was 52.6 versus 42.7 months (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56–0.94).
evidence.limitations: Randomised open-label trial in a selected prior-treatment population. This PFS estimate is investigator assessed and must not be mislabeled as the original primary-endpoint analysis. Population medians are not individual forecasts. All-grade ILD/pneumonitis was 16.7% with T-DXd in this longer follow-up.

evidence.title: DESTINY-Breast04: previously treated HER2-low advanced breast cancer
evidence.population: 557 patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after one or two previous chemotherapy lines; 494 had hormone-receptor-positive disease. T-DXd versus physician's-choice chemotherapy.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Blinded-central-review PFS in the hormone-receptor-positive cohort; PFS and OS in all patients were key secondary endpoints.
evidence.interpretation: In the HR-positive cohort, median PFS was 10.1 versus 5.4 months (HR 0.51). In all patients, median PFS was 9.9 versus 5.1 months (HR 0.50) and median OS 23.4 versus 16.8 months (HR 0.64). These are the original 2022 analysis, also reproduced in EMA SmPC §5.1.
evidence.limitations: The HR-negative subgroup was much smaller. The trial does not establish benefit for HER2 IHC0 tumours or every earlier treatment setting. Drug-related ILD/pneumonitis occurred, including fatal cases; benefit must be discussed alongside pulmonary risk.

cycle_rows.label: Enhertu infusion
cycle_rows.text: Day 1 infusion; next dose normally three weeks later.

cycle_rows.label: Nausea may be delayed
cycle_rows.text: Symptoms vary and can continue after infusion day. Use the prescribed prevention/rescue plan; this band is not a prediction of daily symptoms.

cycle_rows.label: Energy and blood counts
cycle_rows.text: Fatigue and low blood counts can affect any part of the cycle. Bloods and symptoms guide the next dose; no guaranteed recovery day is shown.

cycle_rows.label: Lung symptoms: report promptly
cycle_rows.text: New cough, breathlessness or fever needs urgent contact on any day, including after earlier well-tolerated cycles.

clinical_notes: NCCP00776v3b remains the eligibility anchor despite broader EMA indications. Do not silently add first-line pertuzumab combinations, HER2-ultralow, other tissue sites or earlier-line HER2-low use.
Every12-week echo is an elapsed-time interval; cycle5/9 mapping assumes uninterrupted21-day dosing. New dysfunction changes the interval and treatment decision.
Grade1 ILD restart needs complete Grade0 resolution; ≤28days permits the same dose and >28days a reduction. Symptomatic Grade≥2 ILD requires permanent discontinuation and prompt corticosteroids.

NCCP expects no dose adjustment in severe renal impairment/dialysis; EMA says requirements cannot be determined. Moderate hepatic impairment also has a source-language difference. The engine flags specialist/pharmacy reconciliation rather than inventing a numeric dose.
Neither current NCCP nor the retrieved EMA SmPC supplies a platelet-specific dose ladder. FBC review remains mandatory; US-label thrombocytopenia instructions are not silently substituted.
NCCP eligibility says age>18 while the indication and EMA say adults. The age18 boundary is flagged for clinical/pharmacy interpretation.
Routine prophylactic steroids for antiemesis and high-dose treatment for ILD serve different purposes; patient information must not imply self-starting ILD steroids.
